title: Read a mail-routing rule
summary: Use Claude Code as a guide to unfamiliar code before asking it to change anything.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor.
features: Read-only source explanation and boundary tracing
prompt: Read route.py. Explain the function to someone new to Python. Give the returned value for 0, 24, 25 and 26. Quote the comparison that decides the boundary. Leave the file unchanged.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as route.py. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: You should see four lines in total, including the function definition. Keep the equals sign in the comparison.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: The explanation should mention the unit, MB, and the exact >= operator. If Claude describes a deployed mail policy, ask it to stick to this fictional function.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Ask where a 25 MB item goes, then change only the comparison in the editor to > and repeat the question.
steps.help: The second reading should move 25 to normal. If the answer repeats the first result, ask Claude to reread the saved file.

check: Original values give normal, normal, large, large.
With > only the third case changes.

title: Turn an inventory into a handoff note
summary: Produce a concise note from a tiny file and retain uncertainty in the source.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor.
features: Reading a local CSV and writing Markdown
prompt: Read owners.csv and create handoff.md. Report the total, how many rows have owners, and the names with missing owners. Treat a blank as unknown. Preserve the display names exactly.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as owners.csv. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: There are four data rows. The commas at the ends of Facilities and Front Desk encode empty fields.
steps.code:
name,owner
Shipping,Ari
Facilities,
Design Lab,Kim
Front Desk,

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: Open handoff.md and find the two counts. If Claude invents owners, ask it to trace every name to a line of the CSV.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Fill the Facilities owner with Lee, save, and ask Claude to rebuild the same note.
steps.help: The total stays four. If Facilities still appears in the exception list, make sure Claude reopened the saved CSV.

check: First run lists 2 owned out of 4, with Facilities and Front Desk unknown.
After the edit, only Front Desk is unknown and 3 rows have owners.

title: Keep a project convention across sessions
summary: Teach Claude one project-specific convention, start a fresh session and inspect whether the convention survived.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor.
prompt: Read CLAUDE.md and write release.md for these facts: version 1.2 fixes a duplicate reminder and has been checked on two devices. Follow the project convention.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as CLAUDE.md. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: The filename is uppercase CLAUDE.md at the project root. Rich-text documents or hidden .txt suffixes will prevent discovery.
steps.code:
For every release note, use exactly these two Markdown headings in order:
## Change
## Verification
Use one plain sentence under each heading.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: The release note should have exactly two headings. If a generic template appears, ask Claude which project instruction file it loaded.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Start a new Claude Code session in the same folder. Ask for release-next.md about a corrected date label, verified on one device, without repeating the convention.
steps.help: The new file should retain both headings in order. If it does not, compare the folder shown in each session.

check: Both documents have Change then Verification.
The second note mentions one device and contains no facts copied from version 1.2.

title: Make address comparison predictable
summary: Use a table of examples to drive a small function that compares addresses.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor. Python 3.
features: Implementing a function from fixtures and running regression checks
prompt: Read cases.tsv. Implement unique_addresses(values) in addresses.py for these rules: trim outer whitespace, lowercase, omit blank entries, preserve first-seen order. Write and run unit tests for every example and an empty list. Use Python’s standard library.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as cases.tsv. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: Keep spaces around the first and last values. If your editor removes them, type them back inside the sample field.
steps.code:
input separated by |	expected separated by |
 A@Example.org |a@example.org|B@EXAMPLE.ORG	a@example.org|b@example.org
 | Z@example.org | 	z@example.org

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: Claude should show a test run with no failures. If it sorts the results, ask for a reverse-alphabetical input that reveals the difference.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Ask Claude to print the result for [" Z@X ","a@x","z@x"," "], then rerun the tests.
steps.help: The first value stays first after normalization. If the result starts with a@x, check whether the implementation sorts a set.

check: The check prints ["z@x", "a@x"].
An empty input produces an empty list.

title: Plan a mail report before editing it
summary: Separate an investigation from implementation so you can correct the policy before it reaches code.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor. Python 3.
features: Plan mode and handoff to an editable session
prompt: In Plan mode, read thresholds.txt and propose three test cases for an integer percentage, including the exact boundary and a missing value. Show expected results. Wait for my decision before editing.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as thresholds.txt. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: Use the Plan mode control in Claude Code before sending the prompt. The three rules must be visible in the same file.
steps.code:
Mailbox quota warning begins at 90 percent inclusive.
Below 90 is OK.
A missing percentage must be UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: You should receive a plan with no new files. If 90 is categorized OK, correct the plan while still in Plan mode.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Switch to a mode that permits edits. Ask Claude to implement classify(value) in quota.py and run its three tests with 89, 90 and None.
steps.help: If no file appears, confirm you left Plan mode. If None errors, require the missing-value case to be handled before comparing numeric values.

check: Plan precedes writes.
89 gives OK, 90 gives WARNING, None gives UNKNOWN.

title: Compare two versions of a sharing policy
summary: Find what changed in the policy and write tests for the changed boundary.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor. Python 3.
features: Comparing documents, extracting decision rules and testing a boundary
prompt: Read policies.txt and explain the one behavior that changed. Implement decide(version, kind, days) using Python and the written policy. Build a test table at days 6, 7, 8 for guests and at day 8 for members, with a result for each edition.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as policies.txt. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: Preserve the different comparison operators. You should be able to point to a single character that changes a guest result.
steps.code:
V1: members ALLOW. Guests ALLOW when days < 7; otherwise REVIEW.
V2: members ALLOW. Guests ALLOW when days <= 7; otherwise REVIEW.
Only member and guest are in scope.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Ask Claude to show the number of differing edition results across the four cases, with the one changed row.
steps.help: Exactly one pair differs. More differences usually mean a member was treated as a guest or an inequality was reversed.

check: Day 7 guest changes REVIEW to ALLOW.
Day 8 guest remains REVIEW, and day 8 member remains ALLOW.

title: Test pagination without contacting a tenant
summary: Build a report that follows a chain of saved pages and detects a broken chain before publishing a result.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor. Python 3.
features: Fixture-driven integration tests and failure diagnosis
prompt: Build paged.py from pages.json. Start at one, follow next until null, deduplicate items in first-seen order, and detect a missing page or repeated page. Print the final JSON list on success. On error, print a clear reason and return a nonzero exit code without printing a partial list. Test both failures with temporary fixtures.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as pages.json. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: Keep page two even though it is empty. Its next value is necessary to reach the last page.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: Ask Claude to run its script against the supplied sample. If it stops after M2, examine how it decides that pagination has finished.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Change the last next from null to "one" and rerun. Change it again to "absent" and rerun.
steps.help: The first failure identifies a cycle, the second a missing page. A repeating run needs a set of visited page identifiers.

check: Success prints ["M1","M2","M3"].
Both malformed chains return failure and neither emits a partial success list.

title: Trace a flaky quota test to its date boundary

features: Regression isolation, precise timestamps and injected reference time
prompt: Read expiry.csv. Write Python tests and a classifier accepting an as_of UTC timestamp. An item is expired at as_of >= its deadline. Use timezone-aware timestamps, show the three results at 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z and verify the exact boundary one second later. No dependence on today’s date.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as expiry.csv. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: The middle deadline equals the reference timestamp exactly. Verify both year values if your editor changes date formatting.

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.

title: Hand off a release with independent evidence
summary: Work from a contract, a prior version and a candidate version. Accept or reject before implementing a repair.
requires: Claude Code signed in on a computer, a new empty practice folder and a plain-text editor. Python 3.
features: Plan, independent checks and a verification handoff
roles: Decide whether to publish an update
prompt: Read release.txt. Write tests independent of the candidate, record before/after results in evidence.md, then repair the candidate in fee.py. Give the reviewer a single local command to repeat every check. Preserve the documented boundary and two-decimal output. Include a case outside the supplied examples.

steps.title: Prepare the sample
steps.text: In the new practice folder, use a text editor to save the following as release.txt. Keep the filename and the sample values exactly as shown.
steps.help: Copy both formulas exactly. The candidate is deliberately wrong and the contract is the agreed reference.
steps.code:
Contract: first two items free. Each additional item costs 1.25 dollars. Whole nonnegative counts only. Use fixed two-decimal amounts. Reject negatives.
Previous formula: max(0,n-2)*1.25
Candidate formula: max(0,n-1)*1.25

steps.title: Run the assignment
steps.text: Open this folder in Claude Code and paste the lab prompt. Read the proposed action and allow the local changes or checks specified in the prompt.
steps.help: Require evidence from a test of the uncorrected candidate. If all results pass immediately, ask to run the original candidate expression against two items.

steps.title: Check the boundary
steps.text: Run the command documented in evidence.md. Ask for outputs at -1, 0, 2, 3 and the added case of 6 items.
steps.help: For 0 or 2 the visible output is 0.00. If 6 produces 6.25, inspect how many free items the candidate subtracts.

check: Candidate originally fails at 2; repaired version yields 0.00 for 0 and 2, 1.25 for 3, 5.00 for 6.
Negative count is rejected and the reviewer command passes.
